messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P0 - model initialize storms and node flaps in eu-central1, model=redwood-proto-v2. Trigger: >40% model init failures within 8m. Channel created.

ryan: taking lead. paging @kira and @sam. grabbing logs and topology.

kira: seeing immediate container crashes during shard mmap, then kube restarting pods. Suspect mixed artifacts in local cache + aggressive precompile path.

sam: Node-level symptoms: GPU driver resets and container OOMs. dmesg shows Xid 31 events on a subset of nodes. Also a bunch of kernel udev warnings.

maria: Im pausing new rollouts to eu-central1 and shifting traffic to eu-west1/asia-east1. Applying temporary route: avoid:eu-central1.

incident-bot: Routing change pushed. Estimated propagation ~ 25s.

alex: Support: which customers are impacted?

olivia: Notifying top affected accounts now: ZenData, Quantify, BrightEdge. Sending short status note: "Were mitigating and investigating; expect updates every 30m."

kira: Dump from model init in one failing pod:

```
[2026-03-18T11:05:12Z] loader ERROR: failed to read shard 4: unexpected EOF
[2026-03-18T11:05:12Z] runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc failed, tried to allocate 300MB -> out of memory
[2026-03-18T11:05:12Z] compile WARN: JIT compile took > 120s, timing out
[2026-03-18T11:05:12Z] fatal: aborting due to SIGABRT
```

kira: two failure classes: (A) shard deserializing EOF/corrupt cached objects; (B) immediate GPU OOMs when mapping large KV shards; plus intermittent long JIT compile durations. Manifests show mixed artifact checksums between origin and edge cache.

sam: From node agent:

```
Mar 18 11:04:59 node-gpu-07 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=5124, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 18 11:05:01 node-gpu-07 kubelet: Container runtime restart: oom_kill, pid=5124
```

sam: Xid 31 usually points to illegal memory access or driver bug; could be triggered by corrupted memory mapping of a bad shard.

maria: Quick mitigation plan: 1) stop auto-warmups in eu-central1; 2) drain flaky nodes; 3) force-fallback to smaller model redwood-proto-v1 for production routes in eu-central1; 4) evict local caches with mismatched checksums.

kira: Implementing 1&3: scheduler patch to prefer redwood-proto-v1 for warms in eu-central1 and to disable speculative compile. Patch:

```
PATCH /internal/scheduler
{ "warmup": { "prefer": "redwood-proto-v1", "speculative_compile": false } }
```

incident-bot: Scheduler config updated. Warmup queue dropping.

ryan: Manually cordoning and evicting 4 suspect nodes. Commands:

```
kubectl cordon node node-gpu-07
kubectl -n inference delete pod init-redwood-proto-v2-xyz --grace-period=0 --force
```

kira: After eviction, OOM spikes reduced. Still seeing ~0.5% shard verification fails on edge cache. Running background checksum sweep and initiating cache re-fetch for mismatched objects.

sam: Inventory shows driver versions inconsistent: some nodes on driver 520.*, others on 535.*. JIT toolchain expecting 535+ which explains slow compile and occasional resets. Initiating controlled node upgrade and drain.

maria: Scheduling driver upgrade for affected nodes. Keeping minimal capacity for fallback model. Upgrades estimated 22m. Applying restart throttle: max 1 warmup restart per node per 15m.

olivia: Customer update: "We've rerouted traffic and are serving a fallback model in the affected region. Some customers may observe model behavior differences and transient latency increases. Engineers are investigating; next update in 45m."

alex: Observability: 5xxs began at 11:04:50 UTC, peaked at 11:06:10. After routing and fallback, 5xxs dropped ~72%. Noted persistent higher latencies for ZenData due to model downgrade.

kira: Hotfix plan: add pre-mmap checksum verification and retry-fetch path before mmap/alloc to prevent mapping corrupted blobs. Suggest hotfix patch for runtime:

```
if (!checksum_ok(shard_path)) {
  fetch_from_origin(shard_id);
  verify_checksum(shard_path);
}
gpu_map(shard_path);
```

kira: Also removing speculative precompile that was causing prolonged JIT pressure. Building hotfix and will canary in eu-west1.

sam: Also rate-limited pod restarts to avoid rapid create/delete loops; autoscaler policy adjusted to prefer steady scale for warmup fleet.

maria: Cache eviction job started: removing suspect objects on local caches in eu-central1 and forcing re-download.

incident-bot: Changes recorded: routing, scheduler fallback, node cordon, cache eviction, driver upgrade plan, restart throttles, runtime hotfix queued.

ryan: Canary in eu-west1 looks clean after 18m: model init succeeded, no JIT timeouts, no OOMs. Proceeding to promote to eu-central1 for drained nodes only after driver upgrades.

sam: Post-upgrade checks: no new Xid 31s on upgraded nodes in last 30m. 5xx back to baseline across services.

olivia: Sent post-incident note to affected customers with details and offer for a technical review. No escalations so far.

kira: Drafting RCA: probable contributors:
- corrupted shards in edge/local caches (checksum mismatch)
- heterogeneous GPU driver versions causing JIT/compile divergence
- speculative precompile/prefetch behavior exacerbating memory pressure

kira: Action items (owners):
- schedule continuous checksum reconciliation job for caches (owner: eng-runtime)
- enforce driver version at provisioning time and add continuous inventory (owner: eng-infra)
- implement pre-mmap verification and safe retry path (owner: eng-runtime)
- cap warmup concurrency and add stochastic backoff (owner: platform)
- improve customer-facing rollback/fallback docs (owner: support)

sam: Moving incident to postmortem channel for write-up. Marking mitigated -> monitoring. Reopen if regressions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. Root cause under investigation (artifact corruption + infra mismatch). Next update in 2h or on new findings.

ryan: Thanks all. Handing off follow-up to @kira (RCA) and @maria (infra enforcement). Closing thread.
